Overall, this seems like it should be a minor improvement to AdcSensor to add a new type, a little bit of thresholding logic, and some new interfaces rather than requiring a whole new daemon, and Dbus IPC between them.

I think if we do that, this design doc simplifies a lot, but please make sure your requirements section is complete, and system level requirements, not design details.

Addressed. Design now proposes extending AdcSensor within dbus-sensors as a minor enhancement (new type, thresholding logic, state interfaces) rather than a separate daemon. This eliminates unnecessary D-Bus IPC and redundant data sources. Requirements section rewritten to focus on system-level behavior, not implementation internals.

Status should not be polled.  Like the rest of dbus-sensors, you would use match expressions, or, as I prefer, just keep everything in one daemon with a branch.  Functionally this is nearly identical to what PSUSensor does with exposing status.

Addressed. Removed polling approach. Battery health logic now uses D-Bus match expressions to listen for PropertiesChanged events on ADC threshold properties (WarningAlarmLow, CriticalAlarmLow), similar to PSUSensor model. Updates are event-driven, eliminating periodic polling overhead.
I don't know why these stray whitespace aren't being clean and/or reported by CI.
Fixed in latest patchset. CI formatting pass removed trailing whitespace.

Just take this out.  There are definitely CMOS batteries represented in EM.  They're represented as ADC and sensors, which might not be what you want (and I'm in support of changing) but saying that they don't exist sets the wrong barckground.
Updated. The background now states existing CMOS battery representation through ADC voltage sensors and thresholds, without implying absence in Entity Manager.
I'm not aware of this, can you elaborate on what is inconsistent about the existing "represent a battery voltage as a sensor" approach? (in your design doc please)
Added explicit explanation that inconsistency is in consumer-side interpretation logic (sensor selection + threshold-to-health mapping), not ADC telemetry itself.
This is already a non starter.  Batteries are different between machines.  Some have no battery.  The idea that we'll come up with a completely common configuration seems unlikely to me.
Updated. The document now keeps platform configuration platform-specific and defines only common runtime D-Bus behavior across platforms.

I don't know how we're expected to reason about potential state when the external consumers are "eventual".  I don't see enough rationale on why what we have right now with voltage-thresholds is insufficient.
+1.  In your requirements section you should enumerate what interfaces you're trying to publish.
Addressed. Requirements and runtime interface sections now explicitly enumerate D-Bus path and interfaces, and external consumer direction for Redfish/IPMI.
You've jumped into design, but this is in the background and references section.  Move to the right section.
Updated. Background is now contextual only; implementation details are in the Proposed Design section.
Done
What does this even mean?  what is a "runtime object" ?  Please put specifics of dbus paths and interface names.
Addressed. Replaced value “runtime objects” wording with explicit D-Bus path and interface names.
Remove.  This is an implementation.  The REQUIREMENT is that you expose detect components at runtime, and expose appropriate battery information to Redfish.
Updated. Removed implementation-detail requirement; requirements now describe system behavior.
Remove.  This is already a default in EM today.  This design isn't changing anything.
Updated. Schema-validation requirement was removed.
reword to "Batteries should be detectable based on FRU, and expose the telemetry only if present", or somthing to that effect.
Updated. Requirement now states batteries should be detectable based on FRU/platform configuration and exposed only when present.
Done
Entity-manager is an implementation detail, not a requirement.  Please keep focused on what the SYSTEM does, not how internal components interact (that is for your design section).
Updated. Entity-manager internal wording was removed from requirements and kept out of system-level requirement statements.

This needs to be more specific.  "Battery state" and "runtime objects" don't tell me what you're trying to surface.  Are you trying to surface capacity information?  Voltage?  Serial number?  Please be explicit, as it changes the design dependent on what you're trying to do.
Addressed. Clarified scope: runtime state object publishes health/availability; voltage remains on existing ADC sensor path.
I'm pretty sure this whole section can be removed once you clarify your requirements.
Updated. Removed non-goals section.
It's almost impossible to review this if we don't know what the user interface looks like.
Updated. Added an initial mapping table from runtime D-Bus state to Redfish and IPMI mapping direction for source unavailable, healthy, warning, and critical conditions.
You can condense this all down to: "Will launch an entity-manager configuration using the latest state of the art in dbus-sensors".
Addressed. Condensed low-level startup detail; high-level flow now aligns with dbus-sensors/AdcSensor approach.

This is where you lose me.  Why wouldn't adcsensor just do this directly?

(repeating) what is a "runtime status".
Updated design to derive battery health directly in dbus-sensors/AdcSensor logic.
Remove.  This is something that got added to some configs incorrectly.  Lets not continue that trend.
Addressed. Removed EntityInstance from proposed fields.
I suspect you need to combine this with Type.
Addressed. Removed DeviceName and kept explicit typed model.

This is far too general, but I don't know how to suggest because it's not clear what kind of battery you're trying to support.

CoinCellBattery might be a way to do it.
Updated. Type now uses a specific example: CoinCellBattery.
This is not a "sensor" therefore it would go in the state namespace, not sensors.
Updated. Battery health object is now defined under /xyz/openbmc_project/state/battery/{Name}. Sensor namespace remains only for voltage telemetry.
Please use embedded mermaid rather than attaching pictures.
Updated. Replaced the attached SVG with an embedded Mermaid sequence diagram in the design doc showing the runtime flow.
Remove.  This is currently a requirement of all EM configs.  We don't need to repeat it.
Updated. The standalone Name uniqueness section was removed.
Remove.  We're not going to debate filenames in a design doc.
Updated. New files and systemd service sections were removed from the design document.
Why are you addressing one comment at a time? Please respond to them all before hitting send. Your current approach sends everyone on review an email for every submitted response you're making.
Thanks for the feedback. I will address all review comments and respond together going forward.
Gentle reminder to review this design and feature !
